articles.title: Quantitative CT Phenotypes and Prognosis in Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema.
articles.abstract: Background Combined pulmonary fibrosis and emphysema (CPFE) has heterogeneous outcomes, and visual assessment or separate measurement of emphysema and fibrosis does not directly identify which structural component predominates in an individual patient. Purpose To determine whether quantitative CT enables objective stratification of CPFE into fibrosis-dominant and emphysema-dominant phenotypes and to evaluate their distinct clinical trajectories and prognostic implications. Materials and Methods This secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter observational study included patients with CPFE enrolled between January 2017 and December 2024. A fixed commercial artificial intelligence workstation automatically segmented the lungs and quantified emphysema and fibrosis on high-resolution CT scans. Participants were classified as having the fibrosis-dominant phenotype when the fibrosis percentage was equal to or greater than the emphysema percentage, and as having the emphysema-dominant phenotype otherwise. Group comparisons used the t test, Wilcoxon rank-sum test, χ2 test, or Fisher exact test. Cox models were used to assess all-cause mortality; C index and calibration were used to assess model performance. Results The study population included 1583 participants (median age, 65 years [IQR, 58-71 years]; 1186 men); 823 (52%) had the fibrosis-dominant phenotype, and 760 (48%) had the emphysema-dominant phenotype. The fibrosis-dominant group had a higher fibrosis percentage than the emphysema-dominant group (median, 18% vs 10%; P < .001), whereas the emphysema-dominant group had a higher emphysema percentage (median, 7% vs 6%; P < .001). During a median follow-up of 2.59 years, 513 deaths occurred. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher mortality after adjustment (hazard ratio, 1.36 [95% CI: 1.13, 1.62]; P < .001). Conclusion Quantitative CT helped identify emphysema- and fibrosis-dominant CPFE phenotypes with different prognoses. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality. articles.title: Endovascular Treatment versus Medical Management for Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion from 24 to 96 Hours.
articles.abstract: Background The role of endovascular treatment (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) from 24 to 96 hours after symptom onset remains uncertain. Purpose To evaluate the functional and safety outcomes of EVT versus best medical management (BMM) in patients with AIS due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) presenting greater than 24 hours to 96 hours (hereafter "24-96 hours") after symptom onset. Materials and Methods Prospectively maintained stroke registries from eight stroke centers in China (September 2020-January 2025) were analyzed in this retrospective cohort study. Patients with intracranial internal carotid artery or M1 or M2 middle cerebral artery occlusion, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 6 or higher, and Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score of 3 or higher who presented 24-96 hours after onset were included, grouped by treatment (EVT vs BMM alone), and followed for 90 days. The primary outcome was functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2) at 90 days. Secondary safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and 90-day mortality. Outcomes were compared using multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), adjusted for demographic and clinical variables. Results Among 308 patients (mean age, 67 years ± 12 [SD]; 202 men), 205 underwent EVT and 103 received BMM. Functional independence at 90 days was more frequent with EVT than BMM (50.7% [104 of 205] vs 28.2% [29 of 103]; P < .001). After multivariable adjustment, the odds ratio (OR) for functional independence with EVT compared with BMM was 3.8 (95% CI: 2.1, 6.8; P < .001); after IPTW adjustment, the OR was 4.4 (95% CI: 2.4, 8.1; P < .001). After multivariable adjustment, the incidence of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (5.9% vs 2.9%; OR, 2.2 [95% CI: 0.6, 8.2]; P = .26) and 90-day mortality (11.2% vs 13.6%; OR, 0.6 [95% CI: 0.3, 1.4]; P = .22) did not differ between the EVT and BMM groups. Conclusion Among Chinese patients with AIS due to LVO presenting 24-96 hours after symptom onset, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes, without clear increases in mortality or symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage. © The Author(s) 2026. Published by the Radiological Society of North America under a CC BY 4.0 license. Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Russell in this issue.

Towards Generalizable and Robust Virtual Staining via Causal Intervention.
articles.abstract: Staining pathological tissue is essential for accurate diagnosis but remains a labor-intensive and time-consuming step in pathology workflows. Virtual staining, which computationally generates images resembling conventionally stained tissue sections, offers a promising alternative by significantly improving efficiency and reducing costs. While recent virtual staining methods have shown impressive performance, achieving strong generalization across datasets and maintaining robustness under heterogeneous staining and acquisition conditions remain major challenges. To tackle this issue, we propose a causal intervention-based training framework to improve the generalization and robustness of virtual staining models. From a causal perspective, pathology images contain pathology-relevant features and pathology-irrelevant nuisance variations. While pathology-irrelevant features vary in form and origin, we present a unified strategy to capture nuisance-related variations without explicitly specifying their particular manifestations. Causal intervention is then incorporated during training to suppress these nuisance-related features, encouraging the model to focus on more stable pathology-relevant signals. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first attempts to enhance the generalization and robustness of virtual staining from a causal perspective. Furthermore, our framework is modelagnostic and can be applied to existing virtual staining models in a plug-and-play manner. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets, staining tasks, evaluation protocols, and experimental settings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. Code will be available at https://github.com/999Q999L999/Causal-Virtual-Staining.

articles.title: One-Step Rectified Flow Reconstruction with Spectral Weighting for Limited-angle Cardiac CT.
articles.abstract: Limited-angle cardiac computed tomography (CT) suffers from severe directional artifacts and resolution degradation due to missing wedges in the frequency domain. Diffusion-based reconstruction methods have demonstrated strong artifact suppression capabilities but typically require iterative sampling at a high computational cost. To accelerate limited-angle CT reconstruction, we propose a rectified-flow framework trained with paired supervision for fast inference. Instead of generating images from Gaussian noise, the model learns a deterministic transport from artifact-contaminated Feldkamp-Davis-Kress (FDK) reconstructions to full-view reference images. A 2.5D slice-context modeling strategy is introduced to exploit inter-slice information while reconstructing only the central slice, improving structural consistency. Furthermore, we introduce a reconstruction-aware spectral loss that applies frequency-domain supervision to an approximate endpoint reconstruction inferred from the predicted flow velocity. By embedding spectral priors into the learning objective and using one-step rectified-flow inference (a single network evaluation), the proposed framework achieves fast reconstruction while preserving image fidelity. Experiments on XCAT simulations and clinical cardiac CT data show superior quantitative performance and substantially reduced inference time compared to the state-of-the-art baselines. A qualitative review by an experienced cardiac radiologist further suggests improved visualization of motion-sensitive coronary structures with reduced motion blur.

articles.title: A Registration-Free and Slope-aware Framework for CBCT-based Dental Implant Planning.
articles.abstract: Precise planning of dental implant placement is crucial for oral rehabilitation, yet current AI-based automated methods heavily rely on accurately annotated data. Prevailing approaches obtain training labels by registering pre- and post-implantation CBCT scans, which suffers from low registration accuracy and limited paired data availability. Furthermore, implant-position prediction can benefit from explicit supervision of implant orientation to guide anatomical feature learning. To address these issues, this paper proposes RegFreeNet, a novel registration-free framework. Motivated by the clinical insight that implant positioning is largely determined by the morphology of neighboring teeth, RegFreeNet learns directly from unpaired post-implantation CBCT scans with masked implant regions, thereby eliminating the dependence on registration algorithm. However, removing implant structures introduces new challenges. The occlusion of the mandibular nerve canal within the masked region raises safety concerns regarding anatomical localization. To tackle this, we design a Neighboring Distance Perception (NDP) module, which combines multi-scale convolutions with graph-based spatial context aggregation to recover anatomical context for implant position prediction . We further introduce a slope prediction branch that shares encoder features with the implant position prediction branch. Auxiliary supervision from reference implant slopes guides shared feature learning through joint optimization of implant position and slope prediction. To validate our method, we contribute ImplantFairy, the first large-scale public dataset for dental implant planning, comprising 1,622 implant-specific CBCT samples. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RegFreeNet achieves state-of-the-art performance. Dataset access: https://github. com/sanjinYoung/ImplantFairy.

articles.title: A Robust Physics-Informed Implicit Neural Representation for Speed-of-Sound Image Reconstruction in USCT.
articles.abstract: As a promising imaging modality, ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) holds significant clinical value by providing quantitative parametric maps, such as speed of sound (SOS), in addition to high-resolution anatomical structures. While full-waveform inversion (FWI) is optimal for high-fidelity SOS reconstruction, its severe non-convexity frequently causes traditional discrete grid-based methods to trap in local minima, yielding anatomical artifacts that hinder clinical translation. Here, we propose POLARIS, an unsupervised continuous neural field inversion framework that utilizes spatial continuity as implicit regularization to stabilize the complex FWI optimization. Tailored to the circular acquisition geometry of USCT, we design a scale-aware radially-modulated polar encoding that effectively mitigates radial-angular sampling non-uniformity. We leverage the deterministic nature of the coupling background velocity to extract anatomical boundaries directly from acoustic signals, serving as a structural prior to preserve tissue integrity. Optimization is facilitated by a stochastic shot-batched optimization strategy, leveraging global parameter coupling to update the SOS field from subset emissions and accelerate convergence. Extensive validations on numerical and in vivo breast and musculoskeletal data demonstrate the POLARIS's higher accuracy and structural fidelity. Comparisons with MRI confirm the high anatomical consistency of the reconstructed SOS images. Notably, the framework maintains robust reconstruction performance under sparse-view configurations, highlighting its potential for accelerated USCT acquisition with reduced measurement requirements.

Histotripsy versus Established Thermal Ablation Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of FDA MAUDE Adverse Event Reporting Patterns.
articles.abstract: Background Histotripsy recently received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance for liver tumors, but long-term safety data remain limited. Purpose To characterize histotripsy-related adverse events (AEs) reported to the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database during the early postmarket period and contextualize findings in comparison to microwave ablation (MWA) and radiofrequency ablation (RFA) during comparable observation windows. Materials and Methods A retrospective analysis of the FDA MAUDE database was conducted. AE reports were analyzed over comparable 24-month postmarket periods: July 2024 to July 2026 for histotripsy, January 2017 to January 2019 for MWA, and January 2016 to January 2018 for RFA. Reports were classified by severity (malfunction, serious injury, and death) and medical problem category. Firth-penalized reporting odds ratios (RORs), relative risks (RRs), and Bayesian modeling using Bass model-derived procedure volumes enabled exploratory denominator-adjusted comparisons. Results Of 570 AE reports initially identified, 506 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis (71 histotripsy [median patient age, 68 years; IQR, 56-76 years] and 435 MWA/RFA [median patient age, 58 years; IQR, 50-67 years]). Serious injury and death occurred in 86% (61 of 71) and 14% (10 of 71) of histotripsy reports versus 20% (89 of 435) and 2% (eight of 435) of MWA/RFA reports. Histotripsy had higher reported odds of serious injury (ROR, 14.24 [95% CI: 6.29, 35.56]; P < .001) and death (ROR, 4.35 [95% CI: 1.08, 24.35]; P = .04). In exploratory analyses using modeled procedure volumes, estimated RRs based on reported events were 6.11 (95% CI: 2.64, 14.11; P < .001) for serious injury and 10.94 (95% CI: 4.73, 25.33; P < .001) for death. Although sparse event counts produced imprecise estimates for some complication categories, histotripsy showed higher reporting odds of renal and urinary complications (P < .001), hemorrhage and vascular injury (P < .001), and gastrointestinal and/or abdominal complications (P < .001) in the full cohort. A sensitivity analysis excluding malfunction-only reports showed similar organ system reporting patterns. Conclusion Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

articles.title: Temporal Trends in High-Risk Benign Breast Disease Detection at Screening Mammography: Results from the Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium.
articles.abstract: Background Nationally representative data comparing high-risk benign breast disease (BBD) detection with digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) versus digital mammography are lacking. Purpose To describe temporal trends in high-risk BBD detection rates at screening mammography in the Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium (BCSC) over nearly 2 decades and to evaluate the association between mammographic modality and high-risk BBD detection. Materials and Methods In this retrospective cohort study using prospectively collected data from the BCSC, screening mammograms obtained from 2005 to 2022 among women aged 40 to 79 years at 97 health care facilities were analyzed; examinations in women with prior breast cancer or mastectomy were excluded. Regression analyses were used to estimate annual percent change (APC) in detection rates, and multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORs) according to mammographic modality. Results A total of 4 469 664 screening mammograms in 1 190 380 women (mean age, 57.3 years ± 10.1 [SD]) were included. The overall high-risk BBD detection rate was 1.11 per 1000 examinations, with no evidence of a temporal trend since 2017 (APC = 5.3% [95% CI: -1.1, 21.9]; P = .09). Atypical ductal hyperplasia detection declined from 2009 to 2017 (APC = -7.4% [95% CI: -12.0, -5.4]; P < .001). Detection of radial sclerosing lesions (APC = 5.4% [95% CI: 3.5, 7.8]; P < .001) and atypical papillary lesions (APC = 19.0% [95% CI: 14.8, 25.1]; P < .001) increased from 2005 to 2022. Compared with digital mammography, DBT was associated with increased detection of high-risk BBD overall (OR = 1.36 [95% CI: 1.24, 1.49]; P < .001), lobular carcinoma in situ (OR = 1.37 [95% CI: 1.02, 1.85]; P = .04), atypical lobular hyperplasia (OR = 1.45 [95% CI: 1.19, 1.77]; P < .001), and radial sclerosing lesions (OR = 2.64 [95% CI: 2.15, 3.23]; P < .001). Conclusion Over the past 2 decades, detection of atypical papillary lesions and radial sclerosing lesions increased, whereas detection of atypical ductal hyperplasia declined. DBT was associated with increased detection of high-risk BBD, including lobular carcinoma in situ, atypical lobular hyperplasia, and radial sclerosing lesions. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Hooley in this issue.

Development of RF Probes and Preamplifiers for MRI at Low Fields.
articles.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) systems operating at low magnetic fields (   B 0  ≲ 0 . 25   T) have experienced renewed interest due to the emergence of portable, point-of-care (POC) scanners, and new approaches to mitigating the intrinsically lower signal-to-noise ratios (SNR). The performance of radiofrequency (RF) components is a large factor in determining overall system sensitivity. In contrast to conventional MRI, at higher fields where SNR is typically sample-noise dominated, many low field (LF) systems operate in a coil-noise dominated regime, requiring careful optimization of RF coil design, conductor losses, and receiver electronics. This manuscript surveys RF coil technologies and associated hardware considerations for MRI systems operating below approximately 0.18T, within the range that we designate as low field in this manuscript (0-250 mT). We begin by revisiting early low-field imaging systems and the historical development of RF coil architectures for large-volume imaging. The fundamental noise mechanisms governing low-frequency MR detection are then examined, including Johnson noise in conductors, sample-induced losses, receiver noise figure, and electromagnetic interference (EMI). Design strategies for improving sensitivity are discussed, including conductor optimization (e.g., Litz wire), coil geometry selection such as solenoidal and saddle configurations, and methods for managing coil bandwidth and quality factor. Recent developments in transmit-receive switching, preamplifier design, EMI mitigation, and coil-preamplifier co-design are also reviewed. Finally, we highlight emerging directions for RF hardware development in low-field MRI, including RF coils for encoding, multi-element receive arrays for parallel imaging, and receiver architectures inspired by related modalities such as magnetic particle imaging and ultrasound. Continued advances in RF coil and receiver-chain design will be essential for improving sensitivity and enabling low-field MRI systems for clinical and research applications.

articles.title: Radiomics-Based Differentiation of Enchondroma from Atypical Cartilaginous Tumour and Chondrosarcoma: A Systematic Review and Appraisal.
articles.abstract: The objective was to systematically review radiomics models that differentiate enchondroma from atypical cartilaginous tumour (ACT) or chondrosarcoma and to appraise their methodological quality and readiness for clinical use. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials and Scopus were searched from inception to 24 October 2026 for radiomic, machine learning or deep learning models applied to CT, MRI, radiography or bone SPECT/CT (PROSPERO registration number withheld for blinded review). Performance was synthesised descriptively, not pooled. Quality was appraised with PROBAST + AI, TRIPOD + AI, the Radiomics Quality Score and METRICS. Fourteen reports representing 13 retrospective cohorts (1447 participants, including 79 control scans) were included; two probably overlapping reports were counted once. Eight cohorts used MRI, three CT, one both and one bone SPECT/CT; three reports evaluated deep learning. Eight reports supplied an exact or derivable 2 × 2 table for one of two clinical targets. Sensitivity ranged from 0.800 to 0.935 and specificity from 0.727 to 1.000; preferred areas under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.801 to 1.000. Development quality concern was high in all reports, and all 22 diagnostic evaluation datasets had high risk of bias. One study used geographically external validation; none was prospective or reported decision curve analysis. Median complete TRIPOD + AI reporting was 48.3%. Reported discrimination was promising but methodologically preliminary and does not establish clinical usefulness; prospective assessment and independent multicentre external validation are required.

articles.title: Beyond specificity: growing evidence from validation of CEUS LI-RADS v2017 and proposed revisions.
articles.abstract: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (CEUS LI-RADS) version 2017 provides a standardized framework for characterizing focal liver observations in patients at high risk for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Although the system has demonstrated clinical utility and is endorsed by the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases, accumulating validation evidence reveals an existing gap that limits the application of CEUS LI‑RADS to liver observations beyond those categorized as CEUS LR‑5 for HCC. This limitation arises mainly from the specificity‑prioritized design of CEUS LR‑5 for HCC, which comes at the cost of sensitivity. In this review, we summarize a group of studies on CEUS LI‑RADS for liver observations, addressing their merits, limitations, and proposals for revision. The proposed modifications are investigational, and have not been incorporated into current guidelines. Our objectives are to reduce misclassification, improve the sensitivity of CEUS LR-5 for HCC while maintaining reasonably high specificity, expand the utility of CEUS LI-RADS to a broader range of liver observations, and ultimately optimize patient management. The 60-s threshold for early washout onset lacks statistical derivation and leads to substantial misclassification of HCC as LR-M (probably or definitely malignant, not necessarily HCC); reported HCC proportions among LR-M lesions range from 41.8% to 86.7%. The definitions of washout degrees (mild vs. marked) are somewhat ambiguous, which cause inter-reader variability, and the absence of objective quantitative metrics. Current discussions regarding potential modification of CEUS LI-RADS v2017 include: (1) shortening the early washout threshold from 60 to < 45 s or other threshold, which markedly improves sensitivity of CEUS LR 5 for HCC with minimal loss of specificity; (2) redefining marked washout as occurring at 3 min or later as an adjunctive criterion; (3) incorporating Kupffer-phase findings when using perfluorobutane (Sonazoid); (4) integrating ancillary features; and (5) considering size-stratified thresholds.

articles.title: Progressive collapsing foot deformity: advances in weightbearing CT imaging and three-dimensional assessment.
articles.abstract: Progressive collapsing foot deformity (PCFD) is a three-dimensional deformity characterized, to varying degrees, by hindfoot valgus, midfoot or forefoot abduction, medial column collapse, peritalar subluxation, and valgus instability of the ankle. Conventional weightbearing radiographs remain the cornerstone of imaging assessment, whereas weightbearing computed tomography (WBCT) enables multiplanar and three-dimensional analysis of osseous alignment and articular relationships under load. This narrative review summarizes WBCT-based methods for the assessment of PCFD, including two-dimensional measurements, three-dimensional alignment parameters, articular distance and coverage mapping, diagnostic performance, and automated segmentation methods. WBCT enables quantification of the different components of the contemporary A-E classification and is valuable for assessing peritalar subluxation and lateral impingement. The Foot and Ankle Offset provides a reproducible measure of global alignment, whereas middle facet subluxation and regional mapping more directly characterize local abnormalities in peritalar relationships. Available evidence indicates that class D parameters contribute to distinguishing symptomatic PCFD from asymptomatic flatfoot morphology. However, published diagnostic thresholds remain dependent on the populations and methods used and should not be interpreted in isolation as diagnostic or therapeutic criteria. Automation substantially reduces the time required for three-dimensional analyses, and initial predictive models demonstrate the feasibility of quantitative preoperative planning. However, interchangeability between methods, external validation of thresholds, establishment of normative values, and longitudinal associations with symptoms and clinical outcomes remain insufficiently established. WBCT should therefore be considered complementary to conventional radiographs and MRI. Its principal contribution lies in the multiplanar and three-dimensional characterization, under weightbearing conditions, of the osseous and articular components of PCFD.

articles.title: Letter to editor on "Abbreviated non-contrast magnetic resonance enterography for Crohn's disease: a reliability study" by Caliendo V et al.
Synthetic Data in MR Spectroscopy: Current Practices, Applications, and Considerations.
articles.abstract: Synthetic data generation has become an increasingly important component of methodological development in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS), particularly in contexts where ground-truth in vivo measurements are limited, noisy, or inaccessible. This review provides a structured overview of current practices in synthetic MRS data generation, with emphasis on the physical, biochemical, and computational assumptions that underpin commonly used models. A decomposition of synthetic MRS data is presented in terms of core building blocks, including basis sets, signal formation models, and metabolite parameter distributions such as concentration and relaxation properties. This framework is extended to advanced components required for realistic data synthesis, including baseline and nuisance signals, spatial encoding effects such as coil sensitivities and field inhomogeneities, k-space sampling and gradient imperfections, as well as sample-specific and temporal dynamics. Beyond single-voxel modeling, synthetic data generation across multiple MRS modalities is discussed, including functional MRS, diffusion-weighted MRS, and spectroscopic imaging, with emphasis on modality-specific challenges such as physiological variability, motion, and confounding signal contributions. The role of synthetic data in clinical and preclinical research, acquisition optimization, software validation, and emerging artificial intelligence applications is further examined, with particular attention to domain shift and representational realism. Current practices in validation, reporting standards, and data accessibility are also reviewed, and key gaps limiting reproducibility and interoperability across studies are identified. Overall, this work provides a unified conceptual framework for synthetic MRS data generation, clarifies underlying assumptions across modeling choices, and outlines open challenges toward improving realism, standardization, and utility in both methodological and translational applications. Conducted by the MRS Synthetic Data Working Group under the Code & Data Sharing Committee of the MRS Study Group of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine (ISMRM), this review encompasses the existing literature, supplemented by the collective experience and in-house methodologies of its contributors, providing a community perspective that extends beyond the published record.

articles.title: B 1 +   Optimization in the Heart at 7 T.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: At 7 T, the short RF wavelength in tissue (∼11 cm) causes destructive interference within the chest, leading to  B 1 +   inhomogeneity and posing a critical challenge for cardiac MRI and MRS. While subject-specific parallel-transmit (pTx) optimization can mitigate this, it requires calibration scans and offline computation. To simplify this process, a static "global" shim was calculated and demonstrated to outperform the default transmit configuration without participant-specific calibration. METHODS: B 1 +   maps were acquired in 12 healthy volunteers at 7 T using an 8-channel 1H torso coil. "Personal" phase-only shims were calculated per subject by minimizing a cost function of  B 1 +   homogeneity and efficiency. The "global" shim was calculated by optimizing performance across the cohort, then validated in six additional volunteers by comparing performance against the native mode. RESULTS: In the validation cohort, the "global" significantly outperformed the native shim. It increased the Mean Transmit Sensitivity by ∼20% and reduced CoV by ∼ 16 %  in the septum. The fixed global shim performance was within 3% of the computationally expensive personal shim for all metrics. CONCLUSION: A fixed, population-derived, global phase shim provides a practical, calibration-free approach for improving cardiac  B 1 +   performance at 7 T. The present results extend previous universal RF-shimming work through prospective evaluation in an independent validation cohort and demonstrate that much of the benefit of personal shimming can be retained without participant-specific optimization. The resulting fixed-phase configuration could also provide a practical route towards implementation on single-transmit hardware for cardiac imaging and spectroscopic applications.

articles.title: GC-ResNet: Interference-Resistant Fine-Grained Classification and Robustness Analysis of Highly Similar Anatomical Structures in Nasal Endoscopy.
articles.abstract: Accurate recognition of anatomical structures in nasal endoscopic images is challenging because of high inter-class morphological similarity and common imaging interference, including specular reflections, bubbles, blur, and abnormal exposure. To address these issues, we present GC-ResNet, an improved ResNet-34 framework for fine-grained nasal endoscopic image classification. GC-ResNet integrates squeeze-and-excitation (SE) modules into residual blocks to adaptively recalibrate channel responses and introduces a bottleneck-style global feature refinement module after the final residual stage to refine high-level contextual representations. Experiments on 6706 unique nasal endoscopic images from eight view categories use a fixed image-level split with separate training, validation, and test sets. Across five training seeds, GC-ResNet achieves a test accuracy of 95.58% ± 0.40% and a weighted F1-score of 95.59% ± 0.39% (mean ± standard deviation), maintaining competitive clean-image performance among the compared models. Stress tests suggest improved accuracy retention relative to ResNet-34 under selected synthetic specular-reflection and bubble-interference conditions, with unadjusted paired 95% confidence intervals for the accuracy differences excluding zero. These results support the potential of GC-ResNet for robust fine-grained recognition in nasal endoscopic images.

articles.title: Prediction of Postoperative Neurological Function Recovery in Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy Using MRI-based Delta-Radiomics Combined with Interpretable Machine Learning Model.
articles.abstract: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM) presents progressive neurological deterioration and highly variable postoperative outcomes, while existing prognostic assessment methods have inherent limitations. This dual-center study developed an interpretable MRI-based delta-radiomics model for individualized CSM postoperative prognosis evaluation. A total of 237 CSM patients from Center 1 and 96 patients from Center 2 who underwent decompression surgery were retrospectively enrolled. The Center 1 cohort was stratified by clinical outcomes and randomly divided into training (n = 165) and internal testing (n = 72) cohorts at a 7:3 ratio, while the Center 2 cohort served as an independent external validation set (n = 96). Radiomic features were extracted from pre- and postoperative T2WI MRI images, and delta-radiomic features were calculated. LASSO regression and spearman correlation analysis were applied to screen core radiomic features, and clinical-routine imaging features. Three prediction models were constructed via five machine learning algorithms. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1-score, and pairwise comparisons performed via the DeLong and McNemar tests. Calibration curves and radar charts were generated to determine the optimal algorithm for each model. Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) analysis were performed to assess clinical benefit and model interpretability. Baseline data were well balanced. 16 preoperative radiomic features, 15 delta-radiomic features, and 5 clinical-routine imaging features were finally selected. The XGBoost-based delta-radiomic model achieved the highest numerical AUCs in the internal test (0.899) and external validation (0.802) sets, demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in AUC compared to both the preoperative radiomic model and the clinical-routine imaging model. The model maintained a balanced performance profile across cohorts. This model maintained a higher clinical net benefit across wide threshold ranges. SHAP analysis identified wavelet-domain texture features as risk factors for poor prognosis, while gradient-domain kurtosis features showed bidirectional regulatory effects. Overall, the MRI-based delta-radiomic model effectively predicts long-term neurological recovery in CSM patients. The delta-radiomic model exhibits a more balanced performance profile and statistically better generalizability. By utilizing routine short-term postoperative MRI (within 7 days), this interpretable model holds promise as an objective tool for early prediction of 12-month postoperative neurological recovery.

articles.title: Beyond Model Stochasticity: External Randomness for Diffusion-Based Unsupervised MRI Anomaly Detection.
articles.abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) in MRI aims to identify abnormal regions through a model trained on normal MR images. Recently, reconstruction-based methods leveraging denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) as base generative models (GMs) have gained attention. These approaches typically compute an anomaly score by measuring the difference between a query image and a single reconstructed counterpart (or low-diversity counterparts). However, these approaches typically struggle to differentiate erroneous reconstructions of normal regions from actual abnormalities. To address this problem, we propose a novel approach that enhances anomaly detection by leveraging statistical discrepancy from high-diversity reconstructions. We employ image inpainting with randomly sampled masks to generate diversified reconstructions. We can produce diverse reconstructions through image inpainting even when the input masks differ only slightly, depending on the information retained in the unmasked regions. By sampling multiple random input masks, we can obtain a diverse set of reconstructions, enabling more reliable distinction between normal and abnormal regions. In abnormal lesions, large discrepancies consistently appear across reconstructions, whereas normal regions exhibit irregular and less pronounced differences. Since existing anomaly definitions often fail to adequately capture statistical discrepancy in inpainted images, we introduce a new anomaly score. We define a pixel-wise anomaly score as the average of the normalized differences between the query image and the inpainted images generated from randomly sampled masks covering the pixel. Experimental results demonstrate that our method, with its reconstruction diversification strategy and novel anomaly score, substantially outperforms existing reconstruction-based approaches.

articles.title: LIVSEG: A Cloud-GPU Web Application for Automated Future Liver Remnant Estimation.
articles.abstract: Accurate estimation of the future liver remnant (FLR) is essential for planning hepatectomy and portal vein embolization (PVE), yet conventional calculation relies on manual segmentation that is time-intensive and dependent on specialized workstations. Thus, LIVSEG was developed as a single-page web application that streams DICOM or NIfTI imaging to a cloud GPU running TotalSegmentator nnU-Net models for automated Couinaud-segment and hepatic-lesion segmentation, with an integrated editor for human review. In a cohort of 60 patients (38 living liver donors, 22 PVE patients; 82 scans), the absolute difference between automated and manual FLR was 3.24 ± 2.69 percentage points (pp) in donors and 4.49 ± 5.14 pp across PVE scans, and the two methods were statistically equivalent within a ± 5 pp margin in all cohorts. Using institutional FLR thresholds, LIVSEG and manual volumetry yielded concordant classifications in 79 of 82 scans (96.3%). Inference was completed in two minutes per case at a GPU cost of $0.014-0.026 per study. LIVSEG allows models to reach clinical workflows while retaining human oversight.

articles.title: VCon-Net: A Cerebral Artery Segmentation Network with Enhanced Topological Connectivity.
articles.abstract: Precise segmentation of cerebral artery from computed tomography angiography serves as a fundamental prerequisite for the clinical evaluation and morphological analysis of cerebrovascular diseases, particularly stroke. However, oversegmentation and undersegmentation routinely compromise topological connectivity and accuracy. This study aims to develop a novel deep learning network to mitigate these challenges, enhancing topological connectivity and accuracy. To enforce topological connectivity, we propose a novel skeleton points distance loss that combines skeleton points with a 3D Euclidean distance field to penalize oversegmentation and undersegmentation via interskeleton point distance constraints. Built upon the U-Net architecture, VCon-Net integrates an axialdynamic convolution module and a multiattention mechanism to enhance the perception of slender arteries and capture spatial-channel-temporal features. A total of 202 cases were included in this study, with 141 cases utilized for model development, 35 for independent testing and performance evaluation, and the remaining 26 analyzed as special clinical cases. On the independent test set, VCon-Net achieved a Dice of 0.8552, a Jaccard of 0.7513, a precision of 0.8568, a sensitivity of 0.8645, with HD95 reduced to 3.16 mm, and β0 error reduced to 2.85. Compared with existing segmentation methods, the proposed framework yields favorable performance. VCon-Net achieves cerebral artery segmentation with enhanced topological connectivity, providing a reliable morphological foundation, which offers an essential morphology basis for downstream clinical evaluations.

articles.title: PanPrompt3D: A Prompt-Guided SAM-Based Framework for 3D Pancreatic Segmentation Across Multi-Sequence MRI.
articles.abstract: Accurate three-dimensional pancreatic segmentation is important for pancreatic assessment, treatment planning, and quantitative follow-up. However, most existing segmentation methods have been developed primarily for computed tomography, and their performance across clinically used magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences remains less well characterized. We propose PanPrompt3D, a prompt-guided 3D segmentation framework adapted from SAM-Med3D for pancreatic MRI. PanPrompt3D combines a hybrid Transformer-CNN encoder, 3D triplet attention, volumetric prompt encoding, a 3D mask decoder, and a volume-aware hybrid loss incorporating explicit volumetric consistency. The model was evaluated on public T1-weighted (T1W) and T2-weighted (T2W) MRI data and an in-house cohort of 285 water-sequence examinations. With five-point prompts, PanPrompt3D achieved Dice scores of 81.66%, 85.03%, and 85.07% on water-sequence, T1W, and T2W MRI, respectively. Compared with SAM-Med3D under the same prompting protocol, paired Dice improvements were 4.70, 5.80, and 4.99 percentage points, respectively, with all three comparisons remaining statistically significant after Holm correction. PanPrompt3D also achieved R2 values above 0.9 between predicted and reference pancreatic volumes. Leave-one-sequence-out experiments showed reduced performance on unseen sequences, while external validation on CrossPan and AMOS demonstrated transfer to independent public MRI data, with a clear performance decrease on the unseen out-of-phase contrast. These findings support PanPrompt3D as a practical prompt-guided framework for multi-sequence pancreatic MRI segmentation while highlighting the remaining challenge of generalization to unseen contrasts.

articles.title: VISION-GAN: Mask Conditioned U-Net GAN with Multi-Scale Auxiliary Supervision for Retinal Fundus Image Generation.
articles.abstract: Retinal fundus imaging is essential for early detection of ocular and systemic disease, but training deep models is limited by data scarcity, privacy constraints, and class imbalance. Existing generative approaches mainly target global realism, with limited control over fine-grained retinal anatomy and lesion patterns. We address this by explicitly conditioning fundus image synthesis on retinal structural and lesion-specific priors. A multi-scale residual attention U-Net segments the blood vessels, optic disc, and exudates, and together with diabetic retinopathy (DR) severity labels are used as conditioning inputs to a mask-guided conditional GAN, effectively coupling discriminative segmentation with generative synthesis. The generator is a U-Net with a multi-path encoder and normalization-based conditioning (SPADE, AdaIN, and FiLM) in the decoder, enabling structural guidance, appearance variation, and disease-aware modulation, while a projection-based discriminator enforces local and global realism. The model is trained with a composite objective that combines hinge adversarial loss with multi-scale region-aware reconstruction and perceptual losses. We evaluate the framework on the APTOS, EyePACS, and Messidor-2 datasets using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), Kernel Inception Distance (KID), Inception Score (IS), Structural Similarity (SSIM), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR). The proposed method achieves low FID, KID, and high SSIM, PSNR on all three datasets and improves the metrics over prior GAN-based fundus synthesis methods on Messidor-2. The downstream classification study performed showed that augmenting APTOS dataset with synthetic images improved ResNet-18 DR grading performance. These results show that anatomically conditioned synthesis from multi-mask priors yields realistic, diverse fundus images that are useful for mitigating data limitations in clinical deep learning.

articles.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Tympanic Membrane Otoscopy Classification: A Patient-Level, Multi-Seed Comparison of CNN and Vision Transformer Architectures.
articles.abstract: Otoscopic assessment of the tympanic membrane relies heavily on the clinician's experience and therefore exhibits inter-observer variability. We compared convolutional neural network (CNN) and Vision Transformer architectures for classifying otoscopic images into five classes (acute otitis, cerumen impaction, normal, perforation and serous otitis) within a patient-level, multi-seed, leakage-resistant evaluation framework. The study included 2534 otoscopic images obtained from 735 patients. A held-out test set of 148 patients (20%) was not used at any stage of model development and was accessed only once, at the end of the study. For the remaining patients, patient-level five-fold cross-validation was repeated with five seeds, yielding 25 evaluations per model. Seven architectures were trained under an identical protocol and compared using the Friedman test with post-hoc Nemenyi analysis and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. Swin-T achieved the highest performance (F1-macro 0.900; 95% confidence interval 0.890-0.910), and the models differed significantly (Friedman p < 10⁻9). This superiority stemmed more from design choices than from the architectural family. The hierarchical ConvNeXt-T (CNN) was statistically equivalent to Swin-T, whereas, under the common protocol, the flat-patch ViT-B/16 ranked among the weakest and most costly models. The difference between the families was small (0.881 for CNN versus 0.887 for Transformer). Temperature scaling, learnt on the validation set, reduced the mean expected calibration error (ECE) from 0.077 to 0.043. Most errors occurred between the visually similar acute otitis and serous otitis classes. Explanation faithfulness was quantified using Deletion and Insertion area under the curve (AUC) metrics. Held-out performance was consistent with cross-validation (difference ≤ 0.043), indicating that the models did not overfit. Hierarchical and locally windowed architectures achieved the best balance between accuracy and computational efficiency. The main limitation of the study is that the data are single-centre and external validation has not yet been carried out.

articles.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Retrospective Motion Detection and Conditional Correction (MDCC): Application to Multi-Gradient-Recalled Echo Quantitative MRI.
articles.abstract: Multi-echo gradient-recalled-echo (mGRE) MRI supports quantitative neuroimaging by enabling voxel-wise T2*/R2*/R2t* mapping for quantitative assessment of tissue damage and magnetic susceptibility imaging. Subject motion degrades these acquisitions by introducing inconsistencies due to phase-encoding steps collected at different head positions. Although the gradient echoes associated with a given phase-encoding line are acquired at practically the same head position, differences in contrast, signal-to-noise ratio, and B0 field-dependent phase evolution cause the resulting artifacts to appear differently across echoes and can bias downstream parametric maps. Existing learning-based retrospective correction approaches often discard complex phase information, treat multiple gradient-recalled echoes independently, and apply correction indiscriminately to both motion-corrupted and clean data. We propose Motion Detection and Conditional Correction (MDCC), a retrospective image-domain pipeline that couples a complex-input volume-level Multi-Echo Motion Detection (ME-MoD) model and a complex-valued Multi-Echo Motion Corrector (ME-MoC) in an iterative detect-correct-re-evaluate loop, where correction is invoked only on volumes flagged as motion corrupted. ME-MoD reweights each echo with a phase-preserving paired complex gate, followed by a shared residual slice encoder, and a selected volume-level aggregator. ME-MoC is a fully complex-valued, factorized U-Net with echo-axis multi-head self-attention at the bottleneck, trained with a T2*-consistency physics loss. ME-MoD attained an AUC of 0.95 and sensitivity of 0.91 on the held-out detection set. At the cohort-level analysis, ME-MoC improved downstream R2* fitting results relative to the motion-corrupted input and 2D U-Net and achieved the lowest numerical R2* root-mean-square error (RMSE) among the evaluated methods, including modest numerical improvement over baseline.

articles.title: A Conventional T1WI-Derived Signal Ratio for Differentiating Granulomatous Prostatitis From Prostate Cancer: A Two-Center Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate whether a signal ratio derived from conventional T1WI can differentiate granulomatous prostatitis (GP) from prostate cancer (PCa) in patients with overlapping PI-RADS findings. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective two-center study included 29 patients with GP and 58 patients with PCa, all pathologically confirmed. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging parameters were analyzed. Inter-reader agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors and construct a combined diagnostic model. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and comparisons were performed using the DeLong test. RESULTS: There was no significant difference in PI-RADS scores between patients with GP and those with PCa (p > 0.05), and all patients with GP were classified as PI-RADS 4-5. The T1 ratio was significantly higher in GP than in PCa and showed the best diagnostic performance among individual parameters, with an AUC of 0.769 (95% CI: 0.662-0.876). In contrast, the T2 ratio and ADC ratio showed limited performance, with AUCs of 0.581 (95% CI: 0.447-0.715) and 0.599 (95% CI: 0.469-0.730), respectively. In multivariable analysis including age, T1 ratio, T2 ratio, ADC ratio, neutrophil count, and PSAD, T1 ratio, neutrophil count, and PSAD remained independent predictors for differentiating GP from PCa. A combined model incorporating these three predictors achieved an AUC of 0.873 (95% CI: 0.797-0.949), significantly higher than that of T1 ratio alone (DeLong p = 0.024). CONCLUSION: T1 ratio provides independent diagnostic value for differentiating GP from PCa in patients with overlapping PI-RADS findings. Combining T1 ratio with neutrophil count and PSAD further improves diagnostic performance, supporting the potential utility of routinely available clinical and MRI parameters for noninvasive diagnosis.

articles.title: Half-Dose Gadopiclenol versus Full-Dose Gadobutrol for Hydrops MR Imaging: Comparison in Contralateral Clinically Unaffected Ears.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Hydrops MR imaging, performed 4 hours after IV gadolinium administration, requires sufficient contrast-agent accumulation in the perilymph to delineate the nonenhancing endolymphatic spaces. The higher relaxivity of gadopiclenol may reduce gadolinium exposure while preserving perilymphatic enhancement and anatomic detail. Clinically unaffected contralateral reference ears provide a standardized reference that minimizes disease-related confounding. We compared half-dose gadopiclenol (0.05 mmol/kg; half the gadolinium dose) with full-dose gadobutrol (0.1 mmol/kg) for hydrops MR imaging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed 90 consecutive patients referred for hydrops MR imaging. Forty-five received gadobutrol (1.0 mmol/mL; 0.1 mmol/kg), and 45 received gadopiclenol (0.5 mmol/mL; 0.05 mmol/kg). Two experienced head and neck radiologists, blinded to clinical findings and contrast agent, independently evaluated the clinically unaffected reference ear. Quantitative endpoints were the signal intensity ratio (SIR) and reference-normalized contrast (RNC); qualitative endpoints were separate delineation of the saccule and utricle and visibility of the 3 semicircular canal ampullae. The prespecified noninferiority margin was 0.5 units, with a sensitivity analysis using 0.25 units. RESULTS: Seventy-one patients were included: 37 received gadopiclenol and 34 received gadobutrol. Nineteen were excluded because of motion degradation, suspected bilateral disease, or abnormal audiometric or MR imaging findings in the reference ear. Mean reader-averaged SIR was 8.15 (SD, 1.51) with gadopiclenol and 7.59 (SD, 1.40) with gadobutrol, yielding a mean difference of 0.56 (95% CI, -0.13 to 1.25). Mean reader-averaged RNC was 7.66 (SD, 1.56) and 6.97 (SD, 1.37), respectively, yielding a mean difference of 0.69 (95% CI, 0.00 to 1.39). Both lower confidence limits exceeded the noninferiority boundary of -0.5; noninferiority was maintained using -0.25. Interreader reliability was excellent for SIR (ICC, 0.915; 95% CI, 0.868-0.946) and RNC (ICC, 0.925; 95% CI, 0.882-0.952). Qualitative assessments showed no significant between-group differences. Where estimable, Cohen κ ranged from 0.66 to 1.00; observed agreement was 97.2%-100% for features with nonestimable κ. CONCLUSIONS: In clinically unaffected reference ears, gadopiclenol at 0.05 mmol/kg provides quantitative perilymphatic enhancement noninferior to that of gadobutrol at 0.1 mmol/kg, with comparable qualitative anatomic delineation. Higher-relaxivity gadopiclenol may therefore reduce gadolinium exposure without compromising reference-ear image quality.

articles.title: Is it tumor burden? A critical analysis of postirradiation lymphopenia in lung cancer patients.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: We examined association between treatment‑induced lymphocytopenia and mediastinal lymph node irradiation in locally advanced non‑small cell lung cancer patients and whether disease extent confounds overall survival (OS) analysis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two cohorts were used: A (165 patients) for method development and B (159 patients) for confirmatory evaluation. Auto-segmented mediastinal structure was used as a substitute for lymph node irradiation in the end-of-radiotherapy absolute lymphocyte count (EoRT-ALC) regression models. Comparative EoRT-ALC models with estimated dose to immune cells (EDIC) were developed. In Kaplan-Meier OS analysis the cohorts were stratified by grade 3+ (G3+) lymphopenia before and after accounting for the disease extent via one-to-one propensity score matching. RESULTS: Multivariable models with mean mediastinum dose and EDIC were comparable (adjusted-R2 0.332 vs. 0.337 and 0.253 vs. 0.252 in the A and B cohort, respectively). There was significant difference (p < 0.001 in cohort A, p = 0.03 in cohort B) in OS between the strata with and without G3+ lymphopenia; in cohort A hazard ratio (HR) was 2.29 with 95 % confidence interval (CI) of 1.39-3.77 and in cohort B HR = 1.68 (95 % CI 1.04-2.71). Both strata with G3+ lymphopenia had significantly greater tumor burden and/or nodal stage. After propensity score matching, there was no significant difference (p = 0.30) between the strata; in cohort A HR was 1.42 (95 % CI 0.72-2.80), in cohort B HR was 1.41 (95 % CI 0.73-2.71). CONCLUSIONS: The data showed no consensus which structure might need to be spared in future clinical trials. Further, the data suggested that the disease extent might be confounding G3+ lymphopenia association with worse patient OS. Potential benefit of lymphocyte sparing dose planning cannot be concluded.

articles.title: Variation in Inferior Vena Cava Filter Retrieval Across U.S. Veterans Health Administration Facilities.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters prevent pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients unable to receive anticoagulation but require prompt retrieval once protection is no longer needed. Despite national safety advisories and multidisciplinary guidelines, IVC filter retrieval remains low in the United States. How much variation underlies low retrieval across Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities has not been studied. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study included Veterans who underwent IVC filter implantation at VA facilities between 2016 and 2023. Veterans who died within 90 days of implantation or lacked 1 year of follow-up were excluded. IVC filter implantation and retrieval were identified using procedure codes in the VA Corporate Data Warehouse. A multivariable Bayesian mixed-effects model estimated risk-adjusted retrieval rates across facilities. Logistic regression was performed to identify specific patient- and facility-level factors associated with non-retrieval. RESULTS: Among 3,670 Veterans (median age 69 years; 95.9% male), retrieval occurred in 10.5% within 90 days, 22.2% within 1 year, and 24.7% overall. Risk-adjusted 1-year retrieval varied widely across facilities: 0-60%. Older veteran age (> 75 years), facility academic affiliation, and Southern census region were associated with lower retrieval, whereas implantation at higher-complexity facilities and pre-COVID years were associated with higher retrieval. CONCLUSIONS: IVC filter retrieval rates among Veterans remain low but exceed those reported in non-VA Medicare cohorts. Substantial inter-facility variation highlights opportunities to standardize structured device surveillance, with clear responsibility for follow-up.

articles.title: Aspiration Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis for Acute Limb Ischemia: A Single-Center Retrospective Observational Comparison Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare aspiration thrombectomy (AT) to catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) for the management of lower extremity acute limb ischemia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective study evaluated patients treated from September 2016 through December 2023. Of 303 patients screened, 110 met inclusion criteria with 54 included within the AT cohort and 56 within the CDT cohort. The primary endpoint was limb salvage at 1 month. Secondary endpoints included technical success, limb salvage, primary patency, and secondary patency. Outcomes were reported through 1 year. RESULTS: Limb salvage at 1 month was achieved in 89% of AT patients and 88% of CDT patients. Technical success was achieved in 98% of AT cases and 89% of CDT cases (P = 0.113). No significant difference in survival was noted for all unweighted limb salvage, primary patency, and secondary patency measures. Procedure time and ICU length of stay were significantly shorter in the AT cohort (114 ± 61 versus 150 ± 70 minutes, P = 0.005; median ICU length of stay, 0 versus 1 days, P < 0.001). Thirty-day adverse events did not significantly differ between cohorts. CONCLUSION: Unadjusted comparisons identified no statistically significant differences in limb salvage rates through 12 months with no significant differences in technical success, thirty-day adverse event rates, primary patency, or secondary patency compared to CDT. Aspiration thrombectomy was associated with shorter procedure time and median ICU length of stay. Results should be interpreted as hypothesis generating and future, prospective studies are needed to further compare these treatment modalities.

articles.title: Ultrasound deep learning for predicting aggressiveness in papillary thyroid carcinoma: an exploratory analysis of transcriptomic correlates.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preoperative assessment of aggressiveness in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is important for individualized treatment decision-making. This study aimed to develop a deep learning (DL) model to predict PTC aggressiveness and, in an exploratory analysis, to assess associations between model-derived imaging phenotypes and transcriptomic pathway signatures. METHODS: Preoperative ultrasound images from 1023 patients with PTC were used to develop a DL model for aggressiveness prediction, and clinical features were further integrated to construct a combined DL-Clinic model. Grad-CAM was applied to generate class-specific heatmaps, and mean Grad-CAM activation intensities were extracted from the whole lesion ROI and its core, marginal, and microcalcification regions. Patients were further stratified according to the DL score and regional activation intensity, followed by exploratory GSEA to assess transcriptomic pathway associations. RESULTS: The DL-Clinic model improved the AUCs to 0.834, 0.759, and 0.750 in the internal validation, external test, and prospective test sets, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified the DL score as the strongest independent predictor of PTC aggressiveness (OR = 3.498, p < 0.001). Grad-CAM analysis showed higher activation intensity in the ROI and all subregions of aggressive cases. Exploratory GSEA suggested that high-risk and high-activation phenotypes tended to be associated with enrichment of pathways related to tumor proliferation, extracellular matrix remodeling, and antigen processing, whereas low-risk and low-activation phenotypes were predominantly enriched in immune-related pathways. CONCLUSION: The DL-Clinic model demonstrated discriminatory performance for the preoperative prediction of PTC aggressiveness. Exploratory imaging-transcriptomic analyses suggested associations between model-derived imaging phenotypes and transcriptomic pathway signatures. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to establish the model's clinical utility, and these exploratory imaging-transcriptomic associations require independent validation.

articles.title: Liver and spleen stiffness by 2D shear-wave elastography for identifying high-risk varices in cirrhosis: a prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the performance of liver and spleen stiffness measurement (LSM and SSM) by two-dimensional shear-wave elastography (2D-SWE) in ruling out high-risk esophageal varices (HRVs) and their utility in predicting other portal hypertension-related gastroduodenal lesions and liver-related events (LREs) in patients with cirrhosis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled consecutive adult patients with cirrhosis undergoing screening esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) between 2023 and 2025 at Chulalongkorn University Hospital, Thailand. LSM and SSM were acquired using 2D-SWE (Supersonic Mach 30) within 2 days of EGD by a single blinded operator. HRVs were defined endoscopically as medium-to-large varices or small varices with red wale markings. RESULTS: 169 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled. Of these, 77 (45.6%) and 40 (23.7%) patients had esophageal varices (EVs) and HRVs, respectively. Leading cirrhosis causes were hepatitis B and C virus (n = 66, 39.1%). At thresholds to maximize specificity while maintaining sensitivity ≥ 90%, LSM < 13.7 kPa and SSM < 37.6 kPa by 2D-SWE could spare EGD in 36.7% and 44.4%, respectively, with corresponding missed HRV rates of 4.8% and 4%. Moreover, 2D-SWE-derived LSM and SSM yielded AUCs of 0.778 and 0.844 for HRVs, 0.742 and 0.785 for EVs, and 0.766 and 0.724 for portal hypertensive gastropathy (all p < 0.001). In multivariate Cox proportional hazards analysis, Child-Pugh score and LSM by 2D-SWE were independently associated with the development of LREs within 1 year. CONCLUSION: LSM and SSM using 2D-SWE may help reduce the need for screening EGD in patients with cirrhosis, with observed missed-HRV rates of 4.8% and 4.0%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of 2D-SWE for variceal risk stratification, particularly where vibration-controlled transient elastography is unavailable. The proposed cutoffs require external validation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: High altitude is associated with reduced bone health index in children: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between residential altitude and bone health index (BHI) in children. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter study, healthy children aged 0-17 years who underwent left hand-wrist radiographs were screened at four hospitals at three different altitudes (Beijing 43.5 m, Lhasa 3650 m, Nagqu 4500 m) between September 2013 to July 2022. BoneXpert automatically generated bone age (BA) and BHI. Regional differences were evaluated overall and by chronological age (CA), BA, sex, and ethnicity. Linear regression models were performed to assess the association between residential region and BHI. RESULTS: In total, 1,132 children (CA: 10.60 [6.00, 15.00] years; male: n = 723, 63.9%; Tibetan: n = 666, 58.8%) were included: 376 from Beijing, 454 from Lhasa, and 302 from Nagqu. After adjusting for age, sex, and ethnicity, the increase in BHI with age was attenuated in Lhasa and Nagqu compared with Beijing in models based on CA (region-by-age interaction β = -0.038 and -0.078, respectively; both p < 0.001) and BA (interaction term β = -0.034 and -0.065, respectively; both p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Higher residential altitude was associated with lower BHI and an attenuated age-related increase in BHI.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided biopsy for osteolytic lesions of the appendicular skeleton without extra-osseous component.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: US-guided biopsy is currently used for soft-tissue tumors or bone tumors with extra-skeletal extension. Percutaneous CT-guided biopsy is the current standard for diagnosing bone lesions, but has significant drawbacks, including radiation exposure, lack of real-time needle evaluation, and limited assessment of intralesional vascularity. We aimed to assess the diagnostic yield and feasibility of ultrasound guidance, with CT-guided biopsies as reference, in osteolytic appendicular bone lesions with cortical thinning or disruption but without an extra-osseous component. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of 100 consecutive patients with osteolytic or mixed-pattern appendicular lesions with cortical thinning or disruption and no extra-osseous component, biopsied at a tertiary orthopedic center between November 2022 and July 2026: 22 under ultrasound guidance and 78 under CT guidance. Diagnostic yield, needle caliber, complications, and radiation dose were evaluated. RESULTS: The cohorts did not differ significantly in demographics or lesion size and depth, whereas anatomical site distribution differed (p = 0.02). The diagnostic yield for ultrasound-guided procedures was 90.9% (n = 20/22; 95% CI: 70.8-98.9%), compared to 75.6% (n = 59/78; 95% CI: 64.4-84.9%) for the CT-guided group (p = 0.15). Needle caliber was significantly smaller in the ultrasound-guided group (predominantly 14 G versus 8 G; p < 0.001). No complications were recorded in the investigational group, with one mild vasovagal reaction among CT controls. Median Dose Length Product in the CT cohort was 141 mGy*cm (IQR, 69-292). CONCLUSION: Our preliminary experience suggests that ultrasound-guided biopsy may represent a feasible complementary approach to CT guidance in selected osteolytic (or mixed) appendicular bone lesions with cortical involvement even without an extra-osseous extension.

articles.title: A markedly hypervascular supratentorial ependymoma treated with preoperative embolization: a rare case report.
articles.abstract: Approximately 70% of ependymomas in children and adolescents arise in the infratentorial compartment. However, ependymomas typically exhibit mild hypervascularity, making marked hypervascularity an atypical. To date, few cases of ependymoma with pronounced hypervascularity have been reported. We present the case of a 19-year-old woman with a vividly enhancing intraventricular mass at the septum pellucidum. Preoperative embolization achieved an estimated 40% tumor devascularization. Gross total resection was subsequently achieved, although the postoperative course was complicated by hydrocephalus requiring treatment and an intraventricular hematoma managed conservatively. Histopathological examination confirmed supratentorial ependymoma, CNS WHO grade 3, not otherwise specified (NOS). This case adds to the limited literature on markedly hypervascular ependymomas and highlights the diagnostic and surgical challenges associated with this rare presentation. Recognition of pronounced tumor vascularity is important for preoperative planning, and embolization may be considered to facilitate tumor resection; however, its clinical benefit cannot be established from a single case.

articles.title: Identifying accuracy-preserving truncation thresholds of the time-attenuation curve in CT perfusion for acute anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion stroke.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify the impact of progressively increasing time-attenuation curve (TAC) truncation on CT perfusion (CTP) parameters in acute anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion (AC-LVO) stroke, and to identify truncation thresholds that preserve quantitative accuracy and the reliability of treatment selection. METHODS: This retrospective study included 113 consecutive patients with acute AC-LVO stroke. CTP datasets acquired at 1.5- or 2.0-second sampling intervals were processed using two fully automated AI-based software packages (CTPDoc and United Imaging). TAC truncation was simulated by sequential removal of terminal frames from full-scan datasets. Using full-scan maps as the reference standard, quantitative deviations were analyzed with Friedman tests and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Qualitative agreement regarding treatment eligibility (based on DEFUSE 3, TRACE-III, and SELECT Late criteria) was assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests and percent agreement. Truncation thresholds were defined as the latest time points showing no significant differences (p > 0.05) and good agreement (ICC ≥ 0.75; percent agreement ≥ 82%). RESULTS: Increasing TAC truncation increased parameter deviations and reduced agreement in treatment selection across four groups. Relative to standardized onset, truncation thresholds were 27 and 28 s for CTPDoc (1.5-second and 2.0-second intervals), and 34.5 and 40 s for United Imaging (1.5-second and 2.0-second intervals). CONCLUSION: Although TAC truncation degrades CTP accuracy and treatment-selection concordance, algorithm- and protocol-specific truncation thresholds exist. Adherence to these thresholds may support reliable treatment selection and reduce unnecessary repeat CTP examinations, thereby preventing treatment delays, cumulative radiation exposure, and contrast load when TACs are partially truncated.

articles.title: Impact of race, sex, and insurance status on outcomes following endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients. Endpoint-specific available observations were used without imputation. Outcomes included expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade, admission and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), discharge and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), treatment-time metrics, and discharge disposition. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for seven clinical and procedural endpoints. RESULTS: Final eTICI grade was available for 493 patients. Successful reperfusion (eTICI ≥2b) occurred in 449 (91.1%), and near-complete reperfusion (eTICI ≥2c) in 309 (62.7%). No demographic or payer variable was significantly associated with either reperfusion endpoint. Poor functional outcome occurred in 344 of 448 patients (76.8%) at discharge and 247 of 376 (65.7%) at 90 days. Black race and Medicare insurance were associated with poor discharge outcome. Female sex, Black race, and Medicare insurance were associated with poor 90-day outcome. Medicare and commercial insurance were associated with non-home discharge. Among 516 patients with available door-to-puncture time, the median was 69 min (interquartile range, 54-91), without statistically significant differences by sex, race, ethnicity, or payer. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing EVT at a single comprehensive stroke center, reperfusion rates were high and were not significantly associated with observed demographic or payer variables. Differences in functional outcomes and discharge destination were observed, but residual confounding, endpoint-specific missingness, and the single-center design limit causal interpretation.

articles.title: Carotid plaque morphology on computed tomography angiography associated with cervical recanalization strategy in acute ischemic stroke with anterior circulation tandem lesions.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine whether carotid plaque morphology on preprocedural computed tomography angiography (CTA) is associated with the cervical recanalization strategy used during endovascular treatment (EVT) of acute ischemic stroke caused by anterior circulation tandem atherosclerotic lesions. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed a prospective single-center database of consecutive adults treated with mechanical thrombectomy within 24 h of last known well between January 2022 and February 2025. CTA features of the extracranial internal carotid artery lesion included plaque composition, occlusion-cap morphology, string sign, and calcification pattern (none, eggshell, or dystrophic). Patients were categorized according to cervical recanalization strategy: aspiration alone or percutaneous transluminal angioplasty with or without stenting (PTA±stent). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with PTA±stent. RESULTS: Seventy-nine patients were included (median age, 68 years). Cervical recanalization was achieved with aspiration alone in 40 patients (50.6%) and with PTA±stent in 39 (49.4%); stents were implanted in 14 patients. Dystrophic calcification was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (38.5% vs. 17.5%; p = 0.038). Dystrophic calcification (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 4.84; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37-17.05; p = 0.014) and male sex (adjusted OR, 4.97; 95% CI, 1.43-17.31; p = 0.012) were independently associated with PTA±stent. Successful intracranial reperfusion was more frequent in the PTA±stent group (89.7% vs. 70.0%; p = 0.029), with no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or 90-day functional outcome. CONCLUSION: Dystrophic calcification on preprocedural CTA was independently associated with the use of cervical PTA with or without stenting in patients with anterior circulation tandem lesions. This finding may help anticipate the potential need for cervical angioplasty and facilitate technical procedural preparation.

articles.title: Endovascular treatment of dural arteriovenous fistulas according to cognard classification: a nationwide registry analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Cognard classification stratifies cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs) according to venous drainage patterns and natural history risk. Its influence on early procedural outcomes in contemporary endovascular practice remains unclear. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using the nationwide DeGIR registry, endovascular interventions for intracranial non-cavernous dAVFs with a documented Cognard grade were analyzed. Because this field was part of the registry form only in 2018, the cohort comprises interventions almost exclusively from 2018. Lesions were grouped into low-grade (Cognard I-IIa) and high-grade (Cognard IIb-V) categories. Generalized estimating equations with a logit link, exchangeable working correlation and robust standard errors, accounting for within-patient clustering, were used to compare pretreatment parenchymal hemorrhage, emergency treatment, procedure-level angiographic occlusion, complications within 72 h and access route between groups. Sensitivity analyses and a comparison with ungraded interventions of the same year were performed. RESULTS: A total of 327 interventions in 283 patients from 68 centers were included; in 2018, 78.9% of eligible intracranial interventions had a documented Cognard grade. High-grade dAVFs had significantly higher odds of pretreatment parenchymal hemorrhage (OR 6.45, 95% CI 2.48-16.67, p < 0.001) and emergency treatment (OR 3.82, 95% CI 1.55-9.35, p = 0.004) than low-grade lesions. Complete angiographic occlusion was achieved in 53.5% of interventions (high vs. low grade OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.69-1.89, p = 0.615; risk difference + 3.2% points, 95% CI - 9.3 to + 15.7). Complications within 72 h occurred in 5.8% of interventions (OR 1.09, 95% CI 0.38-3.08, p = 0.874; risk difference + 0.5% points, 95% CI - 5.1 to + 6.0). Results were consistent in sensitivity and adjusted analyses. CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide registry cohort from 2018, higher Cognard grade was strongly associated with pretreatment parenchymal hemorrhage and emergency treatment. No statistically significant association with procedure-level occlusion or 72-hour complications was observed, but confidence intervals were wide and do not exclude clinically relevant differences. These findings describe early procedural results and do not establish equivalent safety or efficacy across Cognard grades.

articles.title: Accelerated Major Singlet Metabolite Mapping in Human Brain Using Nonwater/Fat-Suppressed Ultrashort-TR FID-MRSI With FID-Encoded IDEAL.
articles.abstract: Free-induction-decay MR spectroscopic imaging (FID-MRSI) with LCModel is a well-established, rapid brain metabolite mapping method. However, multislice whole brain coverage still entails substantial acquisition time. To enable water-referenced absolute mapping of the major brain singlets (total choline/creatine/N-acetylaspartate [tCho/tCr/tNAA]) with substantially reduced scan time, we developed nonwater/fat-suppressed ultrashort-TR FID-MRSI (uMRSI) combined with FID-encoded Iterative Decomposition with Echo Asymmetry and Least-squares estimation (IDEAL), a least-squares chemical shift separation framework using uniformly sampled FID points as temporal encodings at 3.0 T. The proposed uMRSI used only 128 FID points shortening TR to 80 ms (vs. 470 ms for conventional FID-MRSI [cMRSI]), yielding 10.58× shorter acquisition for water-referenced quantification. To reduce bias in major singlet quantification from nonnegligible spectral contributions, the FID-encoded IDEAL signal model also included glutamine-glutamate complex (Glx) and myo-inositol (mI) as singlet surrogates, in addition to tCho, tCr, and tNAA. Unsuppressed water and fat were suppressed using an orthogonality-based subspace-projection framework. Macromolecule (MM) basis functions were parameterized from metabolite-nulled data and incorporated into a two-stage FID-encoded IDEAL scheme that jointly estimated metabolite amplitudes, MM contributions, and local field offset. Phantom validation used healthy adult-range metabolite concentrations with added simulated MM; in vivo evaluation (n = 15) compared uMRSI + FID-encoded IDEAL with cMRSI + LCModel. The theoretical number of signal averages (NSA) approached the maximum for the five modeled metabolites. In phantom, major singlets showed low mean absolute percentage error (MAPE; 12.73% ± 3.76%) and Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB; 5.50% ± 1.80%), despite visually noticeable frequency-domain residuals. In vivo, tCho/tCr/tNAA maps showed moderate agreement versus cMRSI + LCModel (structural similarity index measure [SSIM] = 0.71/0.82/0.87; r = 0.67/0.69/0.62 [all p < 0.001]) with small Bland-Altman biases (-0.42/-1.20/-1.98 mM). The proposed uMRSI + FID-encoded IDEAL has potential for further accelerated, water-referenced absolute mapping of the major brain singlets at 3.0 T.

articles.title: Fat Fraction Mapping in the Presence of Magnetic Field Inhomogeneities With Phase-Cycled bSSFP at 3 T.
